t:
(a) In General.—Chapter 129 of title 28, United States Code, is amended by inserting after section 2044 the following:“§ 2045. Investment of court registry funds“(a) The Director of the Administrative Office of the United States Courts, or the Director’s designee under subsection (b), may request the Secretary of the Treasury to invest funds received under section 2041 in public debt securities with maturities suitable to the needs of the funds, as determined by the Director or the Director’s designee, and bearing interest at a rate determined by the Secretary of the Treasury, taking into consideration current market yields on outstanding marketable obligations of the United States of comparable maturity.“(b) The Director may designate the clerk of a court described in section 610 to exercise the authority conferred by subsection (a).”
. 
    (b) Technical and Conforming Amendment.—The table of sections for chapter 129 of title 28, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following:

“2045. 
Investment of court registry funds.”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that a "request" from one official to another is a form of consultation or coordination. It fails because every actor here (the Director of the Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts, a designated court clerk, and the Secretary of the Treasury) is inside the federal government. The section involves no outside party, public comment, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue.
fable.s: may request the Secretary of the Treasury to invest funds received under section 2041 in public debt securities

opus.w: The only interaction here is the Director of the Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts (or a court clerk the Director designates) asking the Secretary of the Treasury to invest court registry funds. Every actor is inside the federal government, so this is coordination within the government, not participation. No public comment, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation, rulemaking or right to sue is created.
opus.s: The Director of the Administrative Office of the United States Courts, or the Director’s designee under subsection (b), may request the Secretary of the Treasury to invest funds received under section 2041 in public debt securities
opus.b: Someone might read this as participation because the Director "may request the Secretary of the Treasury" to invest funds, which looks like one party consulting another before a decision. That reading fails: the Director of the Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts, the Secretary of the Treasury and court clerks all work inside the federal government. No outside party is involved, and the section does not call for rulemaking or a hearing.

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes the Director of the Administrative Office of the United States Courts (a federal entity) to request the Secretary of the Treasury (another federal entity) to invest funds. All actors involved are inside the federal government. There is no requirement to consult or coordinate with any outside parties such as states, tribes, the public, or private organizations.
qwen_chat.s: The Director of the Administrative Office of the United States Courts, or the Director’s designee under subsection (b), may request the Secretary of the Treasury to invest funds received under section 2041 in public debt securities
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "Director's designee" or the "clerk of a court" represents an outside party participating in the decision. However, the Administrative Office of the United States Courts and federal court clerks are part of the federal judiciary, which is considered inside the federal government for the purposes of this definition. The interaction is strictly between federal entities (the Director of the Administrative Office and the Secretary of the Treasury). There is no consultation with states, tribes, the public, or private entities.
